Air Environment
The community in the vicinity of the airport has already been subject to or constructed around major transportation facilities. The existence of other freeways already within the area, the presence of airport and air generated ground and air travel, and the transitioning of land uses from agricultural to residential and industry has already made its impact. The Airport Spur and development at and around the airport is expected to lead to more intensive use of the area with a significantly heavier total traffic but should not cause significant deterioration of air quality in the area.
To the extent that the proposed spur provides for smooth, rapid flow of traffic to the airport relieves connection on other heavily traveled streets in the area, the construction of the Airport Spur will improve air quality.
The air quality analysis summary as presented in Section IV shows that the air quality impact of the Airport Spur project, after construction, will be minimal. In spite of projected increases in traffic, the control of vehicle emissions imposed on new vehicles will result in improving air quality conditions within the study area and Milwaukee County whether the project is built or not.
The microscale level of the air analysis indicates an increase in carbon monoxide concentrations immediately adjacent to the proposed Airport Spur. In no case, however, will these levels exceed the National Ambient Air Quality Standards, significantly degrade air quality or exceed those limits set by DNR.
